title: Seeing vs. Believing: Evaluating the Language Bias of Open-Source MLLMs in Counter-Intuitive Scenes
abstract: arXiv:2601.07737v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance in mainstream visual understanding tasks, but their ability to process action scenes that contradict everyday common sense remains undertested. To address this gap, we introduce CAIT, a benchmark comprising 400 high-fidelity synthetic scenes focused on counter-intuitive visual actions, such as ``a rabbit is chasing a tiger'', where visual evidence explicitly contradicts common-sense expectations. We evaluate human, leading proprietary models (e.g., Claude and Gemini), and 14 representative open-source MLLMs. Humans achieve near-perfect performance (around 0.95 accuracy) and proprietary models demonstrate robust understanding (achieving up to 0.88 accuracy), standard open-source instruction-tuned models perform at the chance level. translated_title: 视觉与信念：评估开源多模态大模型在反直觉场景中的语言偏差
translated_abstract: arXiv:2601.07737v3 公告类型：替换交叉 摘要：多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）在主流视觉理解任务中表现出色，但它们在处理与日常常识相矛盾的场景方面的能力仍未得到充分测试。为填补这一空白，我们引入了CAIT基准，该基准包含400个高保真合成场景，专注于反直觉的视觉动作，例如“兔子追赶老虎”，其中视觉证据明确违背常识预期。我们评估了人类、领先的专有模型（如Claude和Gemini）以及14个代表性的开源MLLMs。人类实现了接近完美的表现（准确率约为0.95），专有模型展现出稳健的理解能力（准确率高达0.88），而标准的开源指令微调模型仅达到随机水平。进一步分析表明，这种失败源于强烈的语言先验：模型倾向于信任语言而非视觉信息。
tldr: 该论文通过新基准CAIT揭示了开源多模态大模型在反直觉场景中因过度依赖语言先验而表现不佳，而人类和专有模型则能有效利用视觉证据。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the CAIT benchmark and reveals that open-source MLLMs fail in counter-intuitive scenes due to a strong language prior, whereas humans and proprietary models effectively rely on visual evidence.
